intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February 2026

experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass
experiences.description: Ski the world-famous slopes of Zermatt with a full-day lift pass covering over 360km of runs with stunning views of the Matterhorn. Book slopes for Days 2-4 to maximize your week after a late Day 1 arrival. Stay in Zermatt village to walk directly to the lifts each morning.

experiences.name: Verbier Freeride Snowboarding Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided freeride snowboarding session on Verbier's legendary off-piste terrain, including the iconic Mont-Fort glacier runs. Schedule for Days 5-6 with a guide who knows the backcountry. Stay in Verbier village center to be steps from the Medran lift station.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Snow Activities
experiences.description: Take the cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m and enjoy snow tubing, glacier walks, and panoramic Alpine views. Plan this for Day 3 as a mid-week highlight. Stay in Grindelwald or Wengen to access the train station within minutes and avoid long transfers.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Mountain Lunch
experiences.description: Enjoy an authentic Swiss raclette and fondue lunch at a traditional mountain hut mid-slope, paired with local wines and regional cheeses. Schedule this for Day 4 during a ski day in Zermatt. Dine at Chez Vrony or Findlerhof, both reachable by ski directly from the slopes.

experiences.name: Matterhorn Glacier Paradise Cable Car and Ice Palace
experiences.description: Ride the highest cable car in the Alps to 3,883m and explore the stunning Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, with sculptures and tunnels. Perfect for Day 7 as a final Alpine highlight before departure. The cable car base is a 5-minute walk from Zermatt village center.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) train from the airport to Interlaken Ost (approx. 2–2.5 hrs, ~CHF 50–60 with a Swiss Travel Pass or second-class ticket). Check in to Bernese Oberland Boutique Stay. Take a short orientation walk around Interlaken town center, stroll along the Höheweg promenade, and get your first iconic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Interlaken old town on foot. Visit a local supermarket (Migros or Coop) to stock up on snacks, breakfast items, and picnic supplies to save money throughout the trip. Settle in and plan the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick bite at the airport (budget CHF 10–15).
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or pretzel at the train station bakery (CHF 6–10).
meals.dinner: Self-catered meal from Migros or Coop supermarket — pasta, bread, cheese, and cold cuts (CHF 8–12 per person). Alternatively, try Goldener Anker in Interlaken for affordable Swiss staples like rösti or spaghetti (CHF 18–25).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Berner Oberland Regional Pass or Jungfrau Travel Pass upon arrival for significant savings on trains, gondolas, and buses throughout the week. Second-class Swiss rail tickets are the most budget-friendly option. Keep receipts for any tourist tax reimbursements.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the hotel, then take the train to Grindelwald (approx. 40 min from Interlaken Ost, ~CHF 10 one-way or covered by pass). Head to First ski area — one of the most accessible and budget-friendly ski resorts in the Bernese Oberland. Rent ski equipment at one of the local rental shops in Grindelwald village (budget rental approx. CHF 35–45/day). Purchase a half-day ski pass for First (approx. CHF 45–55 for adults).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing or snowboarding on the First ski slopes. First offers runs for all levels including beginner-friendly blue runs and intermediate red runs. Enjoy the stunning panoramic views of the Wetterhorn and Eiger. Take a break at one of the mid-mountain self-service restaurants with a packed lunch to save costs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Interlaken by train. Rest at the hotel, then head out for a budget dinner in Interlaken.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel using supermarket supplies — bread, cheese, yogurt, and fruit (CHF 3–5).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket eaten on the slopes — sandwiches, energy bars, and a thermos of hot tea (CHF 5–8).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schuh in Interlaken or Brasserie 17 — try a budget Swiss dish like cheese fondue for two (CHF 20–28 per person). Alternatively, grab a döner kebab or pizza slice from a takeaway in Interlaken (CHF 12–16).

day_by_day.notes: Book ski rentals online in advance for discounts of up to 20%. Wear moisture-wicking base layers and bring sunscreen — alpine UV rays are intense even in winter. Helmets are strongly recommended and usually included in rental packages.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train from Interlaken Ost to Lauterbrunnen (20 min, ~CHF 7 or covered by pass), then the cable car up to Mürren — a stunning car-free mountain village at 1,638m. Explore Mürren on foot and take in the breathtaking views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. Visit the free viewpoint platform near the village center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Schilthorn ski area accessible from Mürren. Ski or snowboard on the Schilthorn slopes (day ski pass approx. CHF 55–65). The area has excellent intermediate and advanced runs. Alternatively, if you prefer a non-ski day, hike the Northface Trail (a winter snowshoe trail) around Mürren for free — snowshoe rental approx. CHF 15–20.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lauterbrunnen and walk through the village to see the famous Staubbach Falls (free, illuminated at night in winter). Train back to Interlaken. Relax at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel (CHF 3–5).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the slopes or in Mürren village. Alternatively, try a bowl of goulash soup at a mountain hut (CHF 8–12).
meals.dinner: Gasthof Hirschen in Lauterbrunnen (affordable Swiss cuisine, CHF 18–25). Or self-cater a warm meal at the hotel using a portable travel cooker or hostel kitchen if available (CHF 8–10).

day_by_day.notes: Mürren is only accessible by cable car and train — no cars allowed, which adds to the charm. The Schilthorn is famous as a James Bond filming location (On Her Majesty's Secret Service). The revolving restaurant at the top (Piz Gloria) is pricey, but the free outdoor viewing platform offers the same 360° views.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in and have a leisurely self-catered breakfast. Then take a free winter walk along the Interlaken lakefront path between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz. The flat 3 km path offers stunning mountain scenery and is completely free. Stop at the Unterseen old town (just west of Interlaken) to see the historic church and medieval buildings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the bus or train to Beatenberg (approx. 30 min, CHF 5–8) and explore the Niederhorn ski and snowshoe area — a quieter and more affordable alternative to the major ski resorts. A half-day ski pass here costs approximately CHF 30–38, making it one of the most budget-friendly options in the region. Enjoy uncrowded slopes and excellent views over Lake Thun.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Interlaken. Visit the Casino Kursaal Interlaken — entry is free and the building is architecturally beautiful. Walk through the illuminated Höheweg in the evening. Head back for a warm dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — oats, fruit, and hot coffee (CHF 3–5).
meals.lunch: Self-service mountain restaurant at Niederhorn — try the daily special (Tagesmenü) which often includes soup and a main for CHF 15–18.
meals.dinner: Metropole Hotel Restaurant has an affordable set menu option. Or try Sandwich Bar Interlaken for a filling and cheap meal (CHF 10–14).

day_by_day.notes: Thursday is often less crowded on the slopes — a great day to take advantage of shorter lift queues. Niederhorn is ideal for families and beginner to intermediate skiers. The views of the Bernese Alps from Niederhorn are often less photographed but equally spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Big day — take the iconic Jungfraubahn cogwheel train toward Jungfraujoch, the 'Top of Europe' at 3,454m. Depart from Interlaken Ost early (around 8:00–9:00am) to avoid crowds. The full ticket is expensive (approx. CHF 145–160 return), but with a Swiss Travel Pass or Jungfrau Travel Pass you get a 25–50% discount. Alternatively, travel only to Kleine Scheidegg (CHF 35–45 return) for stunning views and free snow activities without the summit price.
day_by_day.afternoon: If going to Jungfraujoch: explore the Ice Palace (free with entry), Sphinx Observatory viewpoint, and walk on the Aletsch Glacier. If stopping at Kleine Scheidegg: enjoy free sledding on the natural snow slopes, snowball fights, and photography of the Eiger North Face. Return to Grindelwald or Interlaken by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner tonight to celebrate the midpoint of the trip. Walk along the Interlaken Höheweg at sunset for golden-hour mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure — energy-dense foods like peanut butter toast and bananas (CHF 3–5).
meals.lunch: Pack a hearty lunch for the mountain — hot soup in a thermos, sandwiches, and chocolate. On-mountain restaurants at Jungfraujoch are very expensive (CHF 25–40+), so a packed lunch saves significantly.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Laterne in Interlaken — known for good-value Swiss-German dishes. Try the Bernese Platter (Berner Platte) — a hearty local specialty (CHF 22–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch tickets online well in advance for early-bird discounts. Dress in very warm layers — temperatures at 3,454m can reach -15°C to -25°C in February. Altitude sickness is possible; ascend slowly and stay hydrated. The Good Morning Ticket (departing before 8:00am) offers a significant discount of approximately CHF 15–20.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Wengen — a car-free village accessible by cogwheel train from Lauterbrunnen (approx. 45 min total from Interlaken, CHF 15–20 or covered by pass). Wengen sits at 1,274m and offers access to the Kleine Scheidegg ski area and the famous Lauberhorn ski runs (site of the World Cup downhill race). Rent equipment in Wengen if needed (CHF 35–45/day) and purchase a ski pass (CHF 55–70/day or multi-day pass for savings).
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski the Lauberhorn area — the long Lauberhorn run (15.8 km) is a must-do for intermediate skiers. Enjoy the classic Swiss alpine village atmosphere in Wengen. Try the free cross-country ski trails (Loipen) near the village if downhill skiing isn't preferred (no pass required, just rental skis at CHF 20–25).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Interlaken. Since it's Saturday, check if there are any free local events, markets, or live music in town. Winter Saturday evenings in Interlaken sometimes feature après-ski events at local bars.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel (CHF 3–5).
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant in Wengen — try the self-service option at Restaurant Männlichen or pack your own lunch (CHF 5–8 packed vs CHF 15–20 restaurant).
meals.dinner: Pizzeria Mercato in Interlaken — good-value pizzas and pasta (CHF 16–22). Or grab a raclette from a street vendor if there's a winter market (CHF 8–12).

day_by_day.notes: Saturday slopes can be busier as weekend visitors arrive. Hit the lifts early (before 9:30am) to beat the queues. Wengen is one of the most charming villages in the Bernese Oberland — allow time to walk the village lanes and take photos.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and pack your bags. Take one last walk along the Interlaken lakefront or up to the Harder Kulm viewpoint via the funicular (CHF 14–16 return, or hike up free in about 1 hour). Harder Kulm at 1,322m offers the classic 'Two Lakes' panoramic view of Lake Thun and Lake Brienz with the Bernese Alps as backdrop — a perfect farewell to the Swiss Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and store luggage at the hotel or Interlaken Ost station (luggage lockers available, CHF 5–8). Do any last-minute souvenir shopping — budget-friendly options include Swiss chocolate from Migros (CHF 2–5), postcards, and small Swiss army knives. Head to the train station for your departure journey.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to your departure airport or onward destination. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, snow sports, and mountain adventures in the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered hotel breakfast or splurge on a café breakfast at Café du Théâtre Interlaken (CHF 10–15).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the train station — a fresh sandwich from the SBB station bakery or Brezelkönig (CHF 6–10).
meals.dinner: Airport or train station meal, or pack remaining supermarket snacks for the journey (CHF 5–10).

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00am — confirm with the hotel. Swiss trains run on a precise schedule; arrive at the platform at least 5 minutes early. Consider buying Swiss chocolate and cheese at Migros or Coop at the station — significantly cheaper than airport shops. Don't forget to validate your train ticket before boarding.

trip_options.title: Classic Swiss Alps, Switzerland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Use morning for any pre-arrival rest or in-flight relaxation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at 13:00, clear customs, and transfer to Bernese Oberland Boutique Stay (approximately 1.5–2 hours by train via Interlaken Ost). Check in, unpack, and get oriented. Take a leisurely stroll through the village to soak in the alpine atmosphere, browse local ski rental shops, and pick up any gear or supplies needed for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the immediate surroundings of your boutique hotel on foot. Visit a nearby slope-side viewpoint for your first dramatic look at the Bernese Alps at dusk. Settle into the alpine mood with a warm drink at the hotel lounge or a cozy local café.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast on the plane or grab a quick bite at Zurich Airport's Marché restaurant upon landing.
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or train station — try a fresh sandwich and Swiss hot chocolate from a station kiosk (CHF 15–20).
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the hotel's in-house restaurant or a nearby mid-range alpine tavern. Try Rösti with mountain cheese and a local Bernese beer. Budget: CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Swiss Travel Pass or regional Jungfrau Travel Pass upon arrival at the airport — it will save money on trains and cable cars throughout the week. Confirm ski rental reservation if pre-booked. Rest well for an active Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Snow Activities — Take the famous cogwheel train from Grindelwald or Lauterbrunnen up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m (approx. 2-hour journey). Arrive by mid-morning to enjoy panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier, Europe's longest glacier. Participate in snow tubing and a guided glacier walk on the plateau.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — visit the Ice Palace, a stunning labyrinth of tunnels and sculptures carved inside the glacier. Browse the Top of Europe visitor center and enjoy the Sphinx Observatory observation deck. Begin the scenic cogwheel train descent back to the valley by 15:00–16:00.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bernese Oberland base by early evening. Visit a local ski equipment shop to fine-tune gear for tomorrow's skiing. Relax with a dip in the hotel's wellness area or sauna if available.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss buffet breakfast at the boutique hotel — muesli, local cheeses, cold cuts, fresh bread, and coffee. Included or CHF 18–25.
meals.lunch: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Mountain Lunch experience at the Jungfraujoch restaurant or a mid-mountain hut — enjoy authentic raclette and fondue with alpine views. Budget: CHF 35–45 per person.
meals.dinner: Cozy dinner at a local Grindelwald or Wengen restaurant. Try Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (veal in cream sauce) with Rösti. Mid-range restaurant: CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Jungfrau cogwheel train in advance online — tickets sell out fast in February. Dress in warm layers (temperatures at 3,454m can be -15°C or lower). The Jungfrau Travel Pass covers the train fare. Altitude acclimatization tip: drink plenty of water and avoid heavy exertion upon arrival at the summit.

day_by_day.morning: Full day of skiing at Grindelwald / First ski area — one of the most accessible and scenic ski zones in the Bernese Oberland. Start with groomed blue and red runs in the morning when slopes are freshly prepared. Take the Gondola to First (2,168m) and enjoy wide, well-maintained pistes with stunning views of the Eiger North Face.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing through the afternoon, progressing to more challenging red and black runs if comfortable. Take a mid-afternoon break on a sunny slope-side terrace. Consider a scenic run down to Grindelwald village for a change of scenery before heading back up.
day_by_day.evening: Return equipment to rental shop if needed and head back to the hotel. Enjoy a well-deserved après-ski session at a local bar — try a Glühwein (mulled wine) or hot Ovomaltine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet — fuel up with porridge, eggs, local yogurt, and fruit before hitting the slopes.
meals.lunch: Slope-side mountain restaurant lunch — try a hearty Bergsteiger Teller (mountain platter) with bread, cheese, and cured meats, or a warm bowl of Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup). CHF 20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range Grindelwald restaurant such as Restaurant Firestarter or a local Stübli. Try Fondue Chinoise (hot pot fondue) for a social and filling meal. CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Rent ski equipment from a reputable shop in Grindelwald village the evening before or first thing in the morning (CHF 40–60/day for skis, boots, and poles). Purchase a day lift pass for the Jungfrau Ski Region (CHF 70–85/day). Apply high-SPF sunscreen — UV radiation is intense at altitude even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Zermatt — Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass experience. Depart early from Bernese Oberland by train (approx. 2.5 hours via Visp/Brig). Arrive by 09:30 and collect your full-day lift pass covering 360km of runs. Begin with the iconic Klein Matterhorn cable car for high-altitude runs above 3,800m with breathtaking Matterhorn views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Matterhorn Glacier Paradise Cable Car and Ice Palace — Ride the highest cable car in the Alps to 3,883m and explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier with ice sculptures and frozen tunnels. Ski back down through varied terrain in the afternoon. Explore Zermatt's charming car-free village streets before catching the return train.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bernese Oberland by early evening (train back approx. 2.5 hours). Rest and recover at the hotel. Optional: enjoy a relaxing soak in the hotel spa or hot tub.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — grab extra fruit or a pastry to take on the train.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch in Zermatt — try the Chez Vrony or a slope-side hut for Älplermagronen (alpine macaroni with cheese and applesauce). CHF 30–45 per person.
meals.dinner: Light dinner back in Bernese Oberland — try a local pizzeria or casual alpine bistro for pasta or a wood-fired pizza after a long travel day. CHF 25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is a long but absolutely worthwhile day trip. Book train tickets in advance via SBB (Swiss Federal Railways) app. The Zermatt lift pass is separate from the Jungfrau region pass — budget CHF 80–100 for the day pass. Zermatt is car-free; electric taxis are available from the train station. Start early to maximize ski time.

day_by_day.morning: Verbier Freeride Snowboarding Experience — Travel to Verbier (approx. 2.5 hours by train and bus). Join a guided freeride snowboarding session on Verbier's legendary off-piste terrain. Even if primarily a skier, this guided experience caters to all snow sport enthusiasts and offers access to some of the most exhilarating untracked powder fields in the Alps. The guide will assess your level and choose appropriate terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the freeride session through the afternoon on Verbier's famous Mont Fort and Les Attelas sectors. Explore the extensive 4 Vallées ski network on groomed pistes between freeride runs. Take in the dramatic views across the Grand Combin and Mont Blanc massifs.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski in Verbier's vibrant village — Verbier is renowned for its lively après-ski scene. Enjoy a drink at a slope-side bar before heading back to Bernese Oberland by train.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — carb-load with bread, eggs, and muesli for an energetic freeride day.
meals.lunch: Lunch included or arranged as part of the freeride guide experience — typically a mid-mountain hut with hot soup, bread, and local specialties. CHF 25–35 if self-pay.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Verbier before the return journey — try La Grange or a local brasserie for Tartiflette (potato, cheese, and bacon gratin) or raclette. CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Verbier Freeride experience requires a moderate to advanced skill level for off-piste terrain — confirm your ability level when booking. Helmets are mandatory and avalanche safety equipment (beacon, probe, shovel) is provided by the guide. Book this experience well in advance as guided freeride sessions fill up fast in peak February season. Budget CHF 150–200 for the guided session plus lift pass.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning skiing or snowshoeing in the Bernese Oberland home area — a well-deserved slower-paced day after two intensive day trips. Choose a scenic snowshoe trail around Mürren or Wengen for a peaceful, non-ski snow activity with spectacular Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau views. Alternatively, enjoy a leisurely ski morning on familiar local runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Mountain Lunch experience (if not done on Day 2) — visit a traditional mountain hut mid-slope for an authentic raclette and fondue lunch with local wine. Afterward, explore the village of Mürren or Lauterbrunnen on foot — browse local artisan shops for Swiss souvenirs, chocolate, and watches.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style evening in the Bernese Oberland village — attend a traditional Swiss folk music evening or yodeling performance if available locally. Enjoy a relaxed final full evening at the boutique hotel.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — take your time and enjoy the full spread before a relaxed day.
meals.lunch: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Mountain Lunch at a slope-side mountain hut — full raclette and fondue experience with local white wine or hot herbal tea. CHF 35–50 per person.
meals.dinner: Special dinner at the boutique hotel's restaurant or the best local restaurant in your area — treat yourself to a three-course Swiss dinner: Bündnerfleisch (air-dried beef) starter, venison or lake fish main, and chocolate mousse dessert. CHF 50–70 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Today is intentionally lighter to allow physical recovery before departure day. Use the afternoon to begin packing and organizing luggage. Purchase any remaining Swiss chocolates, cheeses, or alpine gifts. Check train schedules for the departure day to Zurich Airport. Confirm flight details for Day 7.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — wake up early for one last scenic walk or a short ski run to say goodbye to the mountains. Take photos of the sunrise over the Bernese Alps from a viewpoint near the hotel. Check out of the boutique hotel and arrange luggage transfer or storage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart from Bernese Oberland toward Zurich Airport or onward destination by train. The journey from Interlaken to Zurich Airport takes approximately 2–2.5 hours — enjoy the scenic Swiss countryside from the train window as a final alpine farewell. Arrive at the airport with ample time for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, snowboarding, glacier walks, and authentic Swiss mountain culture.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy a full Swiss spread one last time before check-out.
meals.lunch: Grab a meal at the train station or Zurich Airport — try Zurich Airport's wide range of restaurants, from quick Swiss bakeries (Brezelkönig) to sit-down options. CHF 20–35.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the train journey plus airport check-in procedures. Swiss trains are punctual — double-check the SBB timetable the night before. Store large ski bags at the hotel or use the Swiss Baggage service (Reisegepäck) to send luggage directly to the airport from the train station — a convenient and affordable Swiss service. Duty-free shopping at Zurich Airport is excellent for last-minute Swiss chocolate and watches.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

meals.dinner: Fine dining at a top-rated local restaurant such as Restaurant Chesery (Gstaad area) or the hotel's own gourmet restaurant — expect dishes like pan-seared Alpine trout, beef tenderloin with truffle jus, and a curated Swiss wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm ski equipment rental or purchase at the hotel concierge before arrival. Allow time to acclimatize to the altitude. Keep the evening relaxed to prepare for a full week of snow activities.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the day with a gourmet Swiss breakfast at the hotel featuring freshly baked croissants, local cheeses, charcuterie, bircher muesli, and artisan coffee. Then embark on the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe experience — board the iconic cogwheel train from Grindelwald or Interlaken Ost, ascending to 3,454m. Arrive at the Top of Europe and enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in guided snow tubing and a glacier walk on the Jungfrau plateau. Visit the Ice Palace — an extraordinary network of tunnels carved entirely within the glacier featuring ice sculptures. Enjoy the Sphinx Observatory viewing deck for unparalleled 360-degree Alpine views.
day_by_day.evening: Return by cogwheel train to the valley. Freshen up at the boutique hotel and head out for a premium dinner at a Bernese Oberland restaurant. Enjoy a nightcap at the hotel's alpine lounge bar.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet hotel breakfast buffet with local Bernese specialties, fresh fruit, pastries, eggs prepared to order, and premium Swiss coffee
meals.lunch: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Mountain Lunch experience — authentic raclette and cheese fondue at a traditional mountain hut at Jungfraujoch, paired with alpine herbal teas and local wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Schilthorn or a comparable fine dining venue in the Bernese Oberland — featuring seasonal alpine cuisine such as venison medallions, rösti with mountain herbs, and a premium Swiss Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly, especially in peak February season. Dress in thermal layers — temperatures at 3,454m can drop to -15°C or below. The Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue lunch can be arranged as part of the Jungfraujoch day package through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Early hotel breakfast followed by a private luxury transfer to Zermatt (approximately 2–2.5 hours from Bernese Oberland). Arrive in the car-free village of Zermatt and take the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise Cable Car — the highest cable car in the Alps — soaring to 3,883m for jaw-dropping views of the iconic Matterhorn peak and surrounding glaciers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the remarkable Ice Palace carved deep inside the Theodul Glacier, featuring stunning ice sculptures, tunnels, and chambers illuminated in ethereal blue light. Afterward, begin your Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass experience — ski the world-famous slopes with access to over 360km of meticulously groomed runs across Zermatt, Cervinia (Italy), and the Klein Matterhorn area. A private ski guide is recommended for first-time visitors to optimize route selection.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski drinks at one of Zermatt's legendary mountain bars such as Hennu Stall or Papperla Pub. Gourmet dinner in Zermatt before the private transfer back to the Bernese Oberland boutique hotel.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Upscale mountain restaurant lunch on the Zermatt slopes — dine at Chez Vrony or Findlerhof, both Michelin-recognized establishments offering local Valais specialties with spectacular Matterhorn views
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Zermatt at Restaurant After Seven or Capri at The Omnia — expect Mediterranean-Alpine fusion cuisine with an exceptional wine cellar; alternatively, a premium dinner back at the Bernese Oberland hotel upon return

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is a car-free village — transfers within the village use electric taxis. Ensure Zermatt lift passes are pre-purchased or arranged through the hotel concierge. The Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car can be affected by high winds; have a flexible backup plan. A private certified ski guide for Zermatt is highly recommended and can be booked through the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely hotel breakfast. Dedicate the morning to a premium ski session on the local Bernese Oberland slopes — areas such as Grindelwald-First, Wengen, or Mürren offer world-class skiing with far fewer crowds than Zermatt. Hire a private ski instructor for a personalized coaching session to refine technique on groomed pistes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing with your private instructor, exploring intermediate to advanced runs. Mid-afternoon, pause for the Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Mountain Lunch at a traditional mountain hut on the slopes — savor authentic Swiss raclette, cheese fondue, alpine charcuterie, and local wines while surrounded by panoramic mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique hotel for a relaxing spa session — indulge in the sauna, steam room, and an alpine rejuvenation treatment. Elegant dinner at the hotel or a nearby acclaimed local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet hotel breakfast with made-to-order eggs, smoked salmon, local Emmental cheese, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Mountain Lunch — traditional raclette and fondue at an authentic Bernese Oberland mountain hut, paired with Fendant white wine and herbal schnapps
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at a Grindelwald or Wengen fine dining restaurant — dishes such as slow-braised Alpine lamb, truffle risotto, and a curated dessert menu with Swiss chocolate fondant

day_by_day.notes: Book the private ski instructor through the hotel concierge at least 2 days in advance. The Bernese Oberland ski areas are interconnected by cable cars and trains — the hotel concierge can provide a tailored ski map. Fondue lunch reservations at mountain huts should be made the evening prior.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the hotel. Private luxury transfer to Verbier (approximately 2–2.5 hours). Upon arrival, meet your certified freeride guide for the Verbier Freeride Snowboarding Experience — one of the most legendary off-piste snowboarding destinations in the world. Begin with a safety briefing, avalanche transceiver fitting, and route planning with your expert guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided freeride snowboarding session across Verbier's iconic off-piste terrain, including sections of the legendary Vallon d'Arby and Mont Fort glacier descents. Experience the thrill of untracked powder runs with the safety and expertise of a certified mountain guide. Take a break at a high-altitude mountain restaurant for hot drinks and light refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at Verbier's vibrant scene — visit the iconic Farm Club or Fer à Cheval for cocktails. Gourmet dinner in Verbier before the private transfer back to Bernese Oberland.

meals.breakfast: Hotel gourmet breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: High-altitude mountain restaurant lunch in Verbier — enjoy hearty alpine cuisine such as beef bourguignon, tartiflette, and mulled wine at a premium slope-side restaurant like La Vache or Chez Dany
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Verbier at Restaurant Sonalon or La Grange — featuring Valais regional specialties including air-dried beef (viande séchée), raclette with Valais wine, and artisan Swiss chocolate desserts

day_by_day.notes: The Verbier Freeride experience requires a minimum intermediate to advanced snowboarding ability. Confirm skill level with the guide company in advance. All avalanche safety equipment (transceiver, probe, shovel) is provided by the guide. Weather and snow conditions will determine exact off-piste routes — the guide will make final route decisions on the day for safety. Book the freeride guide at least one week in advance as top guides are in high demand during February.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed late breakfast at the boutique hotel — a well-earned rest morning after the intensity of the Verbier freeride day. Enjoy the hotel spa facilities including the heated outdoor pool (if available), sauna, and steam room. Optional: a gentle snowshoe walk through the surrounding alpine forest with a private guide for a peaceful immersion in the winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Bernese Oberland ski area for a final premium ski afternoon — focus on scenic, leisurely runs and take time to absorb the extraordinary mountain panoramas. Consider a scenic gondola ride to a high viewpoint for photography and reflection. Visit a local artisan alpine shop in the village to browse Swiss watches, chocolates, and handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell gala dinner at the finest restaurant available in the Bernese Oberland — request a private dining room or chef's table experience through the hotel concierge. Celebrate the week with a champagne toast, a multi-course tasting menu, and a premium Swiss wine pairing. End the evening with digestifs by the hotel fireplace.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury hotel breakfast — take your time with a full spread including eggs Benedict, smoked meats, artisan cheeses, fresh juices, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Casual but refined slope-side lunch — a gourmet picnic basket prepared by the hotel and enjoyed at a scenic mountain viewpoint, featuring local charcuterie, artisan bread, cheeses, and a thermos of mulled wine
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner — multi-course tasting menu at the hotel's finest dining option or a nearby Michelin-starred restaurant; courses may include amuse-bouche, foie gras terrine, pan-seared Lac Léman perch, wagyu beef with black truffle, artisan Swiss cheese board, and a decadent chocolate soufflé with Valais ice wine

day_by_day.notes: Reserve the chef's table or private dining room at least 3 days in advance. The hotel concierge can arrange a custom gourmet picnic basket with 24 hours' notice. This day is intentionally lighter on activities to allow physical recovery before departure day and to savor the final full day in the Alps.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely gourmet breakfast at the boutique hotel. Pack and check out — the hotel concierge will arrange luggage handling and storage if needed. Take one last walk through the alpine village or a short scenic cable car ride for a final panoramic farewell view of the Bernese Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury chauffeur transfer to the airport or onward destination. Depending on flight time, stop en route in Interlaken or Bern for a brief city stroll, Swiss chocolate shopping at Läderach or Sprüngli, or a final Swiss coffee at a lakeside café.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry home exceptional memories, Swiss chocolates, and perhaps a new passion for the Alps.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet hotel farewell breakfast — indulge in all favorites one last time, including fresh pastries, Swiss cheeses, local honey, bircher muesli, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch en route to the airport — either a premium airport lounge meal or a stop at a high-quality Swiss restaurant or bakery in Bern or Interlaken such as Confiserie Tschirren or Restaurant Della Casa
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dinner depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange luggage transfer the evening before. Allow at least 3 hours before international flight departure for airport procedures. Swiss airports (Zurich, Geneva) offer excellent luxury shopping and dining in premium departure lounges — consider lounge access through credit card benefits or direct purchase. Ensure all ski equipment rentals are returned before departure.
